title: The Camel That Wouldn't Walk
summary: A family's desert trip comes to a sudden stop when their camel refuses to move, until the children patiently discover the small, hidden cause and solve it together.
poll: When an animal suddenly behaves strangely, it is usually just being stubborn, not trying to tell you something.

versions.title: The Camel That Wouldn't Walk
versions.text:
Lama and Yousef went on a desert trip with their family. Their camel's name was Saqr.

Saqr carried their bags. He walked and walked. Then he stopped. He would not walk at all!

Their father pulled the rope. Saqr did not move. Their mother called his name. Saqr did not move.

Yousef gave him some food. Saqr ate it. But he still would not walk!

"Maybe he is just stubborn," said Lama. But she wanted to look closer.

Lama looked at Saqr's feet. Yousef looked too. They were patient. They checked each foot.

Then Lama saw it. A small, sharp thorn was stuck in Saqr's foot!

Yousef pulled the thorn out gently. Saqr lifted his foot. Then he took a big step.

Saqr walked again! The whole family laughed and clapped. Saqr was happy too.

Lama knelt down. She looked at Saqr's feet. Yousef knelt down too. They checked each foot. They were very patient.

Yousef gently pulled the thorn out. Saqr lifted his foot. He shook it. Then he took a big step forward.

Saqr walked again, right across the desert! The family laughed and clapped. Saqr seemed happy too.

Saqr carried the heavy bags. He walked across the sand for almost an hour. Then, without warning, he suddenly stopped. He would not take another step.

Their father pulled gently on the rope. Saqr did not move. Their mother called his name softly. Saqr just stood there.

Yousef gave him a handful of dates, hoping that would help. Saqr happily ate the dates. But he still would not walk!

"Maybe he is just being stubborn today," said Lama, trying not to laugh. Still, she wanted to look closer before giving up.

Lama knelt down in the sand. She looked closely at Saqr's feet. Yousef knelt beside her. Together they checked each foot. They were very patient.

Then Lama saw something small and sharp. It was poking out from Saqr's foot. It was a tiny, stubborn thorn!

Yousef gently pulled the thorn free. Lama held Saqr steady. The camel lifted his foot. He shook it. Then he took a long step forward.

Saqr walked happily across the desert again! The family laughed with relief and clapped. Saqr seemed pleased too.

versions.title: The Camel That Wouldn't Walk
versions.text:
Lama and Yousef were thrilled to go on a desert trip with their family. They packed bags onto their camel, a big brown camel named Saqr. Saqr had carried the family's things for many years.

Saqr carried the heavy bags. He walked steadily across the sand for almost an hour. Then, without warning, he suddenly stopped. He would not take another step.

Their father pulled gently on Saqr's rope. The camel did not move. Their mother called his name softly. Saqr just stood there, stubborn as ever.

Yousef offered a handful of sweet dates, thinking food might change his mind. Saqr happily ate every date. But he still would not walk another step!

"Maybe he is just being stubborn today," said Lama, trying not to laugh at the silly moment. Still, something made her want to look closer before anyone gave up.

Lama knelt in the sand. She examined Saqr's feet carefully. Yousef knelt beside her. Together they checked each large, padded foot. They stayed very patient and gentle.

Then Lama noticed something small and sharp. It was poking out from between the pads of Saqr's foot. It was a tiny, stubborn thorn, hidden where no one would easily see it.

Yousef gently pulled the thorn free. Lama held Saqr steady. The camel lifted his foot, shook it, and took a long, confident step forward.

Saqr walked happily across the desert once again! The family laughed with relief and clapped for joy. Saqr seemed just as pleased as everyone else.

Lama and Yousef were thrilled to go on a desert camping trip with their family. They loaded bags onto their camel, a tall brown camel named Saqr. Saqr had carried their things for many years.

Yousef offered a handful of sweet dates, hoping food might change the camel's mind. Saqr happily ate every date. But he still refused to walk another step!

"Maybe he is just being stubborn today," said Lama, trying hard not to laugh. Still, Saqr kept shifting his weight. That made her want to look more closely before giving up.

Lama knelt in the warm sand. She examined Saqr's feet carefully, watching for any small gesture that might explain his discomfort. Yousef knelt beside her. Together they checked each large, padded foot. They stayed very patient.

Then Lama noticed something small and sharp. It was poking out from between the pads of Saqr's foot. It was a tiny, stubborn thorn, hidden exactly where no one would notice it.

Yousef gently pulled the thorn free. Lama held Saqr steady. The moment the thorn came out, the camel lifted his foot, shook it, flicked his ears in a happy gesture, and took a confident step forward.

Saqr walked happily across the desert once again! The family laughed with relief and clapped, realizing Saqr had not been stubborn at all. He had simply been trying to tell them something was wrong.

Yousef tried offering a handful of sweet dates, hoping food might change the camel's mind. Saqr happily gobbled up every date, but he still refused to walk another step!

Camels are remarkably well suited to desert life. Their wide, padded feet spread out across loose sand, which usually protects them from sharp rocks and thorns scattered on the ground. Even so, on rare occasions, a thorn can still slip beneath the tough pad and cause real discomfort.

Yousef gently pulled the thorn free while Lama held Saqr steady. The moment the thorn came out, the camel lifted his foot, shook it, flicked his ears in a happy gesture, and took a confident step forward.

Saqr walked happily across the desert once again! The family laughed with relief and clapped, realizing Saqr had not been stubborn at all. He had simply been trying, in his own quiet way, to tell them something was wrong.

LOW.prompt: Why do you think it was a good idea for Lama and Yousef to check Saqr's feet instead of just saying he was stubborn? Use at least two facts from the story.
checklist: I clearly said what I think.
I used at least two facts from the story.
I wrote complete sentences with capital letters and periods.
LOW.modelAnswer: I think it was a good idea. If they had just said Saqr was stubborn, the thorn would still be stuck in his foot. Instead, they looked closely at his feet and found the thorn. Because they checked carefully, they were able to pull it out and help Saqr feel better.

keyWords.definition: refusing to change your mind or do something, even when others want you to

keyWords.definition: able to wait calmly without getting upset or giving up

keyWords.definition: to look at something closely and carefully

keyWords.definition: a feeling of being a little hurt or uncomfortable

keyWords.definition: a small movement of the body that shows a feeling or message

MID.prompt: Explain how Lama and Yousef solved the mystery of why Saqr stopped walking. Use at least two details from the story about what they did.
checklist: I explained how the mystery was solved.
I used at least two details from the story.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: Lama and Yousef solved the mystery by staying patient and looking closely at Saqr instead of simply calling him stubborn. They knelt down and examined each of his feet carefully, watching for any small gesture that might explain his discomfort. That careful examination led Lama to notice a tiny thorn stuck between the pads of his foot, which Yousef then gently pulled out.

HIGH.prompt: The story shows that patience and close observation revealed a problem that frustration alone would have missed. Do you agree that this lesson applies beyond animals, to how people solve problems with each other too? Support your argument with evidence from the story, and address a counterargument.
checklist: I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that this lesson applies well beyond animals. In the story, Lama's perseverance and empathy let her notice a thorn that the rest of the family had missed while simply pulling the rope and calling Saqr's name. Someone might argue that in a real emergency there is no time for such patience, but the story suggests the opposite: it was precisely because Lama slowed down and looked carefully, rather than reacting with frustration, that the real problem was found and solved quickly and safely.
